Pay people right, and on time
“Give the worker his wages before his sweat dries.”
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ · Sunan Ibn Majah 2443

Fourteen centuries ago, that teaching made a simple point that every business owner still feels today: when someone has done the work, they have earned their pay, and holding it back is a wrong. Payday isn't paperwork. It's rent, groceries and peace of mind for the people who keep a business running.

Yet for many small businesses, payroll is the hardest part of having a team. Software is expensive, tax rules change every year, and employees wait on HR just to see a pay stub. Mistakes and delays land on the people who can least afford them.
WageHarbor gives a small business the tools a large one takes for granted:

a clear calculate → approve → pay flow, with a direct-deposit file ready for your bank.
every employee can see, print and save their own pay stubs and balances, any time.
each company's data is kept apart, and sensitive numbers are encrypted.
Paying correctly and promptly is the most concrete way a business shows respect for its people.

How we protect your payroll data
Payroll holds some of the most sensitive information a business has. Here's how WageHarbor looks after it.
Every company's data is kept separate

Each company on WageHarbor has its own private space. Every request is limited to the signed-in person's company at the data layer, and changes to another company's records are refused. People at one company can never see another company's employees, pay or settings.
Viewing a full Social Security number is recorded in the audit log.
Passwords are never stored. Only a salted, one-way hash is kept, using ASP.NET Core Identity.
The right people see the right things
Employees only ever see their own pay, time and details.
with an authenticator app, plus recovery codes.
for password-free sign-in on supported devices.
Sessions are re-checked every 30 minutes, so someone whose sign-in is disabled is signed out of any open session within that time.
The audit log records who changed company settings, employee records, pay setup, payroll runs and tax tables, and when, so mistakes and misuse can be traced.
